reports.reviewer_notes: Provisional (C, AI stand-in) view only — not a screening decision. Cross-sectional comparison of self-reported habitual exercisers (EX) vs sedentary (SED); no identifiable single bout, so charted as background per v3 contract 2.5 (resting cross-sectional training studies unchanged from v2), not Core A/B. Blood drawn fasting, mornings only, over a 12-month recruitment window; time since each participant's last exercise session is NR. See unresolved_questions re: the companion bioRxiv preprint (not downloaded) and the extent of extraction warranted for a background-classified multiomics report.
author_window_interpretation_locator: Whole paper (Abstract p.1; Discussion p.12-13) frames findings in terms of regular/habitual exercise's long-term immunometabolic remodeling; no acute post-exercise bout, immunosuppression/open-window, or redistribution framework for a single exercise session is discussed anywhere in the text.

cohorts.cohort_label: CIMA natural-cohort subset meeting activity-questionnaire eligibility, split by self-reported habit into EX (n=40, regular exercisers) and SED (n=46, sedentary controls)
cohorts.baseline_health: Nonobese (BMI < 30 kg/m2) Chinese adults aged 20-40 y, self-reported absence of active infection and pregnancy at CIMA recruitment; this study additionally excluded smokers and individuals with a history of cancer or chronic infectious disease (e.g., tuberculosis)
cohorts.age_sex: Combined EX+SED mean age 28.2 ± 3.1 years; SED group predominantly female (statistically significant sex imbalance vs EX, exact % NR in main text, see fig S1A); BMI 21.3 ± 3.0 kg/m2
cohorts.training_status: EX: planned, structured exercise ≥3 times/week, accumulating ≥150 min/week moderate-intensity or ≥75 min/week vigorous-intensity activity (WHO Guidelines-based self-report); SED: self-reported zero purposeful exercise per week, 'sitting' as primary daily posture
cohorts.sport: NR (exercise mode/type not specified beyond 'planned, structured exercise')
cohorts.cohort_notes: 428 CIMA enrollees -> 314 met activity-questionnaire eligibility (after excluding those with missing activity-questionnaire responses) -> 86 analyzed in this study (EX 40 + SED 46); participants reporting low-intensity-only or below-WHO-threshold moderate/vigorous activity were excluded from analysis entirely to maximise EX/SED contrast. Not all 86 had complete data across all omics modalities (exact per-modality n given only in table S1, not reviewed in this extraction).
cohorts.age_range: 20-40 years (CIMA/this-study recruitment inclusion criterion); analyzed 86-subset mean 28.2 ± 3.1 y (SD), no min-max given

measurements.platform: CellChat (R package) cell-cell communication inference on scRNA-seq data
measurements.comparison: EX vs SED, relative information flow and differential interaction number/strength
measurements.effect_measure: relative information flow; communication probability; interaction number/strength
measurements.effect_value: total interactions: SED=766, EX=777 (Fig.6A); THBS, IL-6, RESISTIN, ICOS signaling higher in SED (i.e. attenuated in EX); CCL, MHC-II, MHC-I, PECAM1, COLLAGEN, CXCL, IFN-gamma signaling higher in EX (Fig.6C); HLA-G-CD8A/B (MHC-I) pair most pronounced increase in EX, driven by cMono/cDC to CD8+ Tn (Fig.6F); IFN-gamma signaling from NKT to myeloid/B cells markedly enhanced in EX (Fig.6G-H)
measurements.effect_unit: communication probability; relative information flow (unitless); interaction counts
measurements.effect_uncertainty: P<0.01 significance threshold shown as dot size in bubble plots (Fig.6E, F, H); no CI given
measurements.multiplicity: NR (CellChat does not apply a stated multiple-testing correction across pathways in this description)
measurements.confounding: NR (CellChat run on the same sex/BMI-adjusted single-cell data but no explicit covariate adjustment described for the communication inference itself)
measurements.reported_feature_count: NR (full pathway list not enumerated in main text beyond Fig.6C ranking)
measurements.measurement_notes: Resistin signaling (myeloid-cell-centred) specifically down-regulated in EX at both the communication-probability level (RETN-CAP1/RETN-TLR4) and the RETN transcript level in myeloid cells (fig S10A-C); authors interpret this as reduced proinflammatory/vascular-risk signaling. Causal relationship between metabolites and these signaling changes is explicitly stated as not tested ('the direct causal relationship between these metabolites and immune cells was not explicitly tested in this study').
supplement_sources: fig S10, not reviewed in detail

source_locator: p.14 col.2 Methods (FDR/BH correction for biochemistry and DEGs)
precision_validation.evidence_notes: QC metrics and batch-effect checks are reported for both single-cell modalities (fig S2A-C, no evident batch effect between EX/SED) and cross-modal annotation concordance was checked (gene-activity-score vs transcriptome). However, the primary metabolomics/lipidomics molecule-selection threshold used nominal (uncorrected) P<0.05, with FDR q-values given only secondarily 'for transparency' — i.e. mixed reliability rigor across platforms; no ICC/CV/technical-replicate reliability estimates reported for any platform.

source_locator: p.13 col.2 Methods 'Assessment of physical activity and grouping'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Cross-sectional resting/habitual design with no identifiable single bout; there is no exercise-end time point to anchor a time_bin, so the organising-window construct does not apply to this report (within_organising_window=NA at the sample_set level). Time since each participant's last exercise session before blood draw is not reported.

Single-cell resolution (scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq) gives lineage- and subset-specific (34/30 subsets) immune-cell readouts rather than bulk PBMC/plasma-only measures, which is a relative immune-specificity strength; plasma metabolomics/lipidomics findings, by contrast, are not immune-cell-specific (whole-plasma matrix) and are only indirectly linked to immune cells via post-hoc narrative (see PV-R01-005).

precision_validation.individualization: Cross-sectional, independent-groups (EX vs SED) design with no repeated within-person measurement; individualization/responder analysis is out of scope for this design, not merely unreported.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Design does not attempt within-person repeatability or individual-threshold estimation at all (between-subject cross-sectional group comparison); coded NA rather than not_demonstrated because the domain is inapplicable to this design, not merely unaddressed within an applicable design.

precision_validation.functional_evidence: not_demonstrated — metabolite/TF/GO findings are annotation- or correlation-based, not direct functional assays (no cytotoxicity/degranulation/stimulation assay performed)
source_locator: p.12 col.2 Discussion: 'Although the direct causal relationship between these metabolites and immune cells was not explicitly tested in this study, these observations provide a robust foundation for hypothesis generation'
p.12 col.2: 'reduced susceptibility to infection documented in physically active populations (5, 58)'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Authors explicitly state the metabolite-immune mechanistic links are hypothesis-generating, not tested; the discussion's claim about reduced infection susceptibility in physically active populations cites external literature (refs 5, 58), not a clinical endpoint measured in this study. No direct functional assay (e.g., cytotoxicity, cytokine stimulation) was performed.

precision_validation.replication: A female-only sensitivity analysis (same cohort, restricted subset) was run to check robustness of DEG/DAR findings against the EX/SED sex-composition imbalance (figs S11-S12); this is an internal robustness check, not an independent-cohort or prospective validation.
source_locator: p.13 col.1 Limitations: 'a female-restricted sensitivity analysis confirmed consistent directional trends in DGE and DAR... figs S11 and S12'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Single cross-sectional cohort (CIMA); no external cohort replication or prospective/implementation validation described for any of the headline findings. The female-only check is a within-cohort confound-sensitivity analysis, not independent validation.

precision_validation.field_feasibility: Resource-intensive workflow fully described (PBMC isolation/cryopreservation, paired scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq, targeted LC-based metabolomics/lipidomics); physical-activity assessment used a low-cost self-report questionnaire explicitly chosen over objective accelerometer measurement, which the authors flag as a trade-off/limitation ('lacks external validation against standardized tools... cannot substitute for objective... measurements').
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Single-cell multiomics + targeted metabolomics/lipidomics is costly/labour-intensive and not field-deployable as implemented; the exposure-classification instrument itself (questionnaire) is low-cost/feasible but explicitly acknowledged as imprecise.
